newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-BALLESTEROS EYES PLACE ON RYDER CUP TEAM.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BALLESTEROS EYES PLACE ON RYDER CUP TEAM.

text.p: Seve Ballesteros, captain of Europe's Ryder Cup team, is refusing to rule out his chances of automatic selection as a player against the United States in September.
His confidence was boosted on Friday in the second round of the Benson and Hedges International when he shot a three-under-par second round 69 containing three birdies and not a single bogey.
It was that second achievement which surprised many. Asked when he last had a bogey-free round, Ballesteros shook his head thoughtfully. "I'm not sure," he said. "Certainly not this year."

Now aged 40 and troubled by a back ailment, the charismatic Spaniard's form has dipped to an alarming degree in the past two years. In seven tournaments on the European Tour this year, he has missed the cut six times, but his two-round total of 141 has ensured him a place in the final two rounds here.

Ballesteros, who is still suffering from back trouble and has to exercise daily, is fully aware that only the top 10 in the Ryder Cup standings are automatic selections. He is currently 29th on the list.
Questioned whether he could close the gap and play his way into the team, Ballesteros bristled. "What do you think? Yes? I think so too! I'm not too far away. If I win here I'll be in the top 10.
"Winning here would do it, or the PGA, or Deutsche Bank Open or British Open. One win. You all laugh. I say I can win the Open -- why not?"
